entities.name: PMID:27506482
observations: Systematic review of seven studies (495 infants ≤32 weeks); suppositories did not shorten time to full feeds; enema evidence conflicted; enemas and rectal stimulation did not shorten complete meconium evacuation.

entities.name: PMID:27050644
observations: Meta-analysis of six RCTs (442 infants): full-feed time MD −0.03 days (95% CI −2.47 to 2.41); low-certainty evidence; no significant NEC difference.

entities.name: PMID:35332357
observations: Meta-analysis of six single-center RCTs (389 infants): glycerin interventions associated with about 1.5 days earlier meconium evacuation, but no faster enteral feeding; evidence very low to moderate.

entities.name: PMID:38648060
observations: RCT in 286 infants born at 23–30 weeks: breast-milk enema versus saline shortened complete meconium evacuation by 2.2 days and full-feed achievement by 4.6 days; no notable safety-outcome differences.

entities.name: PMID:28768263
observations: Pilot RCT of 61 VLBW infants: saline washout versus glycerin suppository shortened time to full feeds by 4.6 days in the 750–999 g subgroup, but not in 1000–1500 g infants.

entities.name: No routine feeding benefit
observations: Across systematic reviews, routine glycerin suppositories and pooled meconium-evacuation interventions have not reliably shortened time to full enteral feeds; evidence is low certainty and underpowered.

entities.name: Breast milk enema signal
observations: One 2024 RCT found breast-milk enemas accelerated meconium clearance and full feeding versus saline in 23–30-week infants; confirmatory multicenter evidence is needed.
